cells.tense: Something is arriving now and you are letting it be here without rushing it into an answer.
cells.ask: Give one settled feeling ten unhurried minutes today, no task attached, and let what it says come on its own.
cells.core:
Something is coming in right now and you are letting it land without needing it to become a decision. Not numbness and not a mood you're nursing — a feeling with depth enough to sit in, that doesn't have to announce itself. That stillness is not passive; it is how what's here gets to be fully in the room.

Being that settled is what lets you stay close to someone without losing where you end, because the feeling is allowed to be what it is before it gets spoken. Today, stay with one quiet thing a little longer than usual. Not to conclude anything — just to let it be here. The feeling is yours already, and holding it takes nothing away from anyone else.
cells.sheetLine: You can let a feeling be here before it becomes a decision.
cells.verb: sitting with what the heart holds, before it moves

cells.tense: You are reaching for a feeling that hasn't arrived yet, bracing for a moment that hasn't been written in.
cells.ask: Let one feeling you have already settled today stay settled, and drop the rehearsal for the next one.
cells.core:
You are straining toward a feeling that hasn't arrived yet. Before it's here you've already decided what it should be, what it will mean, how the other person will take it — and you're living in that imagined version while the real moment is still at the door. The pushing spends the calm the moment needed.

Letting feeling settle is what lets you tell where the other person actually is, not where you need them to be. Charging ahead of it turns closeness into a forecast. Today, one thing you already feel is allowed to simply be that — no rehearsal, no next move. Letting it be finished is what opens the space for the next true thing.

cells.tense: A moment when feeling could have entered came and went, and you are still at that old threshold.
cells.ask: Say one thought out loud to someone today, even a small one, and let them hear it without pre-clearing it first.
cells.core:
Something was meant to come in and you were there when it did — but the welcome didn't happen. A tenderness or a knowing has been waiting and you've kept it on the far side of the line. That old threshold is still where you're standing, even though the day has moved on.

Feeling lands and then gets shared, small and unpolished, without needing to be certain first. So today, gather one thought that's been sitting with you and say it plainly to one person, listening for what comes back. You're not reaching for a feeling here. You're letting one thought cross the line and find out it can be met.

cells.tense: Something is already moving through you and settling, and you are calling it just how you are.
cells.ask: Name one quiet feeling that shaped what you said or did today, and own it as yours, not the room's.
cells.core:
There is a settled feeling running in you and shaping how you take things in — you can see it in what you let pass and what you hold close — and you describe it as if it were just how you happen to be. The feeling is doing real work; the claim that it came from you hasn't been made.

When that claim is in place, you can be close to someone without dissolving into them, because you know the feeling started on your side and not in the room. Let one quiet impression from today be fully named as yours — not as proof of anything, just as the truth of what moved through you. That name is what keeps the closeness clean.

attempts.check: The one claim the record does not support if stated flatly is that the person knows, or can identify, what feeling is entering — the kernel says the seat recognises what is arriving, not that they have named it. A reader could reasonably say the feeling is not settled or is actively stirred, not still; a Reverie read can overclaim contentment. The asks survive being wrong because each is a small act done with what is actually at hand, not a verdict on their inner state. The sentence that would serve the writer — 'you already know what this feeling is' — is the one left out; the cells say 'something' instead.
